title: A 195-event audit did not resolve the change in assigned-depth share for global M5.5+ ComCat events in 2000-2025
abstract: We used a prior 195-event metadata audit to estimate assigned-depth shares for 12,848 global M5.5+ ComCat events. We weighted eight era-by-depth groups by their catalog sizes. Missing method labels could be assigned or not assigned. Estimated assigned shares were 68.53-87.90% in 2000-2012 and 44.64-49.98% in 2013-2025. The estimated change range favored a decrease. But conservative simultaneous 95% sampling limits for change were -71.21 to +26.25 percentage points. These limits require the fixed hash ordering to behave like random sampling within groups. After exact 10, 33 and 35 km depths were removed, change limits also included both signs. Large other-depth groups had only 25 checks per era and many missing labels. Thus this audit did not resolve the direction of the global metadata change under the stated method. This is a new weighted uncertainty analysis of prior source snapshots, not independent data confirmation. It does not test true depth or physical shallowing. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure, reproduction steps and a separate numerical audit are included. External event records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Population-weighted assigned-depth shares. Blue ranges allow missing labels to take either class. Gray limits allow sampling uncertainty under the hash-as-random assumption. They have at least 95% simultaneous coverage under that model.

citations.reason: Reuses the source inventory and 195 external detail snapshots. New weighted finite-population uncertainty analysis; no independent event sample.
Prior depth-spike study motivates the question; same bulk snapshot.
